reachable: Yes, and I verified it by execution rather than by reading. The mechanism is data-side, so \"receives gradient\" is not the right test — the test is whether the batch composition measurably differs from uniform in the regime the harness runs. It does. Instrumented copy of the impl under bs=64, total_steps=4000, n=2304 (the real train size, from cloud/podresults/g0-02-causal-variance-film.json:198 `n_train_seqs: 2560`, minus the dev split at eval/adapter.py:186): realized n_hard matches the hypothesis formula exactly at every step I probed (step 1 -> 0, 100 -> 3, 600 -> 16, >=1200 -> 32 of 64), and after the ramp every batch carries 8 groups of 4 distinct sequences drawn from one bucket. I confirmed by reconstruction that every member of every emitted group really carries the bucket's (image, normalized-path, depth) signature, and that all members of a group share the image. The reweighting the batcher applies to sequences is real but modest (per-sequence marginal 0.63x..1.52x of uniform). The mechanism reaches the scored read only through the trained weights, which is the only route a batcher has; there is no direct path to the scored position and none is claimed. I also verified the mechanism's premise on real data end-to-end: `fit` dicts do carry `cmds` and `image` (realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:83, preserved through cloud/build_context.py compose_train_seqs and evolve/harness.py _strip_target_only), so the tracker is not silently falling through to its image-only degenerate path — on the real sample it recovers 74 routed reads across 24 sequences with depths {1:50, 2:12, 3:4, 4:8}. The collision premise is confirmed on real data, not assumed: bucket ('alpine:latest', '/tmp/w/cvar/g#/acc.dat', 1) contains real sequences 0, 5 and 16, and sequences 0 and 5 both issue the byte-identical command `cat /tmp/w/cvar/g2/acc.dat` with entirely different observations ('cv-d6821fdc...' vs 'cv-a27924b7...'). The partner objective r22 forms an n-by-n distance matrix over all command rows in the batch (evolve/chunks/objective/r22_exact_target_equivalence_quotient.py:60-93), so it does consume the in-batch pool the batcher composes — the hypothesis's \"the partner's stack is the one in front of me that does\" is true.
summary: The code does what the hypothesis says it does. Every mechanical claim checks out under execution: the symbolic tracker implements the stated mv/cp/redirect/read rule table verbatim (impl lines 76-94); `_norm_path` reproduces the hypothesis's own worked example exactly ('/tmp/w/cups/g53/f149.tmp' -> '/tmp/w/cups/g#/f#.tmp'); demand is the sum of capped depths over routed reads while signatures are a set, exactly as described; bucket weight is size^size_pow * exp(depth_beta*depth) and member weight is 1+demand with without-replacement draws; the key begins with the image so every group is a same-system block (verified on emitted groups, not inferred); n_hard follows the stated linear ramp to the digit; the batch is permuted; and the contract holds — deterministic given seed, global torch RNG untouched, `fit` unmutated, exactly bs in-range indices with no repeats. Cost is as claimed: 0.045 s to construct at n=2304 and 0.59 s for all 4000 sampling steps. Two of the author's three named risks resolve in the code's favour on the real data — the parser handles 100% of the cat/mv commands (only `ls` is skipped, correctly), and normalized shapes do recur (11 of 51 buckets already hold >=2 distinct sequences at n=24, with the collision premise confirmed by two real sequences issuing byte-identical read commands with different contents). The third risk, dispersion, is the one that bites: the realized Force 1 is a depth-mix tilt (d4 share of sampled routed reads 10.8% -> 15.6%), not the claimed shift of mass toward routed reads (their share of sampled steps actually falls, 0.1022 -> 0.0974), because the batcher can only reweight whole sequences and the harness trains on every step of a sampled sequence. That is a divergence in the stated causal story, not in the code. Caveat on my method: the only real training data in reach is the 24-sequence jail sample, so the reweighting numbers come from that population tiled to n=2304 — the tiling preserves the batcher's relative bucket and member weights exactly, but it cannot tell me how well the deep cups path-shape buckets populate at the true n, and I did not verify that.

divergences.claim: "Weighting buckets by exp(depth_beta * depth) and members by 1 + demand raises the effective weight of exactly the steps whose target is only predictable by carrying a content identity across a move, at the expense of ambient ls/uname/cat steps that are predictable from the command string alone." (hypothesis.txt:70-73, Force 1)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The batcher samples whole SEQUENCES, and the harness feeds every step of a sampled sequence into the loss (evolve/harness.py:83-88: collate of the full sequence, cmd_mask over all command rows). So the reweighting cannot select steps; it can only reweight sequences by their routed-read density. Measured on the only real training data available (evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl, 24 verbatim train sequences, tiled x96 to n=2304 — tiling preserves the batcher's relative bucket weights exactly, since size^0.5 scales by a common 96^0.5 and member weights are unchanged), the routed-read share of sampled steps does not rise; it falls slightly. What the code actually realizes is a shift in the DEPTH MIX of routed reads, not a shift toward routed reads.

divergences.claim: "The tracker assumes whitespace-separated commands ... Commands it cannot parse are skipped, which under-counts depth rather than mis-counting it, so the failure is a weakened signal rather than a wrong one." (hypothesis.txt:110-112)
divergences.what_the_code_does: Skipping is not always under-counting. _routed_reads only mutates `hops` on a parsed event, so an unparsed `mv A B` leaves hops[A] intact; a later `cat A` would then be labelled a routed read at A's stale depth even though A no longer exists. That is a mis-count, not an under-count. It is vacuous on this data — the only unparsed verb is `ls` (106 of 724 commands), and every `cat` and `mv` in the real sample parses — so the claim's practical conclusion ("weakened, not wrong") holds here even though its stated reason does not.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/batcher/r2_routed_collision_depth_batcher.py:76-94. Executed over all 24 real train sequences: `total cmds 724 unparsed by verb: Counter({'ls': 106})`; verb census of the whole sample is `Counter({'cat': 446, 'mv': 172, 'ls': 106})` and every mv is a 2-argument absolute-path form.

divergences.claim: "bs - n_hard uniform slots, drawn iid exactly as the parent does" (hypothesis.txt:35-36)
divergences.what_the_code_does: The uniform slots are drawn by rejection from a 3*need randint block, conditioned on not colliding with the hard slots or with each other, so they are uniform-without-replacement and slightly anti-correlated with the hard half — not iid, and not the parent's single randint(0,n,(bs,)) call. The same sentence goes on to state the rejection, so this is self-contradicting phrasing rather than a hidden behaviour. A final tail loop (line 182-183) appends without rejection and could emit duplicates, but only in a regime unreachable at n=2304/bs=64.
